CRMO patients have reduced anti-inflammatory cytokines and increased pro-inflammatory cytokines, and that these changes are related to the impaired ERK1/2 signaling pathway.
CRMO monocytes are characterized by reduced anti-inflammatory and enhanced pro-inflammatory IL10-related cytokine production.

we identified a novel mechanism for CRMO, namely that CRMO monocytes show an imbalance in IL-10-related family cytokine expression that results in NLRP3-inflammasome activation and IL-1β release, which may contribute to the chronic inflammation and bone loss in CRMO patients.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the IL10 family cytokines have a complex role in the inflammatory response and that their expression is tightly regulated in order to maintain immune homeostasis.

altered IL10 family cytokine expression in monocytes from patients with chronic recurrent multifocal osteomylitis results in enhanced IL-β expression and release, contributing to inflammatory bone loss.

altered expression of IL-19, and to a lesser degree, IL-10, in CRMO monocyte cells, results in enhanced expression and release of pro-inflammatory IL-1β, which may contribute to inflammatory bone loss in CRMO patients.
